hero.headline: Trump says Israel must accept any Iran deal, calls for immediate ceasefire
hero.body:
President Trump asserted his authority over Middle East negotiations, telling the Financial Times that Israel will be forced to accept whatever agreement the United States reaches with Iran. "I call all the shots. He doesn't call the shots," Trump said, referring to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The statement came as Israel and Iran engaged in direct military strikes for the first time since a ceasefire took effect in April. Israel targeted petrochemical facilities in Mahshahr that produce materials for ballistic missile development. Iran responded by backing its proxy Hezbollah after Israeli military operations escalated in Lebanon.

Trump called for an immediate halt to hostilities on Truth Social, posting that "Israel and Iran must immediately stop shooting" and urging both sides to stand down as regional tensions mounted.

The Trump administration's approach signals a significant shift in US policy toward Israel. By publicly stating he controls negotiations regardless of Israeli objections, Trump indicated the administration intends to pursue talks with Iran without requiring Israeli approval. This contrasts with previous administrations that granted Israel substantial influence over Iran-related decisions.

However, divisions have emerged between the Trump administration and allied nations over ceasefire terms. Vice President JD Vance clarified in Budapest that Lebanon was not part of the Iran ceasefire agreement, despite apparent misunderstandings. He stated: "I think the Iranians thought that the ceasefire included Lebanon, and it just didn't. We never made that promise."

British officials have publicly disagreed with this position. Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper told BBC Radio 4 that continued Israeli strikes on Lebanon were "completely wrong" and emphasized that "Lebanon must be included in the ceasefire." Defence Secretary John Healey similarly called for ending the Israel-Lebanon conflict as part of broader ceasefire terms.

Britain also expressed concerns about Trump's suggestion that Iran could charge tolls for passage through the Strait of Hormuz. Healey warned that introducing any pay-for-passage system would create a dangerous precedent for international shipping and contradict established maritime law. He said such an arrangement "simply isn't sensible and isn't actually doable."

The escalation in Lebanon has intensified since the April ceasefire announcement. Israeli bombing campaigns have continued with significant casualties, while Iran responded by halting oil tanker passage through the Strait of Hormuz. The blockade of this critical shipping route has affected global fuel and fertilizer prices, with ripple effects on economies worldwide.

Cooper emphasized in her remarks to City leaders that freedom of navigation through international waterways underpins global trade and security. The renewed hostilities and diplomatic disagreements between the Trump administration and its traditional allies suggest that achieving a sustainable ceasefire agreement faces considerable obstacles, despite Trump's insistence on American control over negotiations.

cards.headline: Zelensky Meets European Leaders as U.S. Steps Back From Ukraine Mediation
cards.teaser: President Volodymyr Zelensky traveled to London to meet with the leaders of Britain, Germany, and France as the United States reduced its role in peace negotiations with Russia.
cards.body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky met with the leaders of Britain, Germany, and France in London to discuss peace negotiations with Russia. The meeting came as U.S. President Donald Trump's focus shifted toward the war with Iran, marking a reduced American role in Ukraine mediation efforts.

During the meeting, Zelensky's European allies set out five conditions for peace talks. The shift represents a significant change in diplomatic efforts, with European powers now positioned to lead negotiations aimed at resolving the conflict.

cards.headline: Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo spreads at unprecedented rate
cards.teaser: Officials report the current Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is spreading faster than previous epidemics in the country.
cards.body:
The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is spreading at an unprecedented pace, according to a warning from the Africa CDC. Officials monitoring the epidemic say the speed of transmission marks a significant escalation compared to previous outbreaks in the central African nation.

The rapid spread of the virus has raised concerns among public health authorities about containment efforts in the region.

cards.headline: FISA Section 702 spy law faces Friday deadline as extension remains uncertain
cards.teaser: The Section 702 surveillance law expires this Friday, with chances of an extension uncertain.
cards.body:
Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act is set to expire on Friday, and the prospects for extending the law remain unclear. The uncertainty is partly attributed to Trump's Director of National Intelligence appointment.

The spy law has been a key tool for intelligence gathering, but its renewal has faced political obstacles. With only days remaining before expiration, Congress has not yet secured the votes needed to extend the program.

cards.teaser: Crude oil prices rose sharply after Iran and Israel conducted attacks against each other, threatening the stability of a recent cease-fire agreement.

The hostilities have raised concerns about potential disruptions to energy supplies from the region and the possibility of broader conflict. cards.headline: Trump considers government stakes in artificial intelligence companies
cards.teaser: The president publicly discussed the possibility of the government taking equity positions in major AI firms as his regulatory approach toward the industry shifts.

President Trump said he is weighing whether the federal government should acquire ownership stakes in major artificial intelligence companies. The president made the comments publicly as his administration's position on regulating the AI industry continues to evolve.

Taking equity positions in private companies would represent an unusual intervention in the market by the federal government, raising questions about the relationship between Washington and Silicon Valley.

cards.headline: At least 32 killed in magnitude-7.8 earthquake in southern Philippines
cards.body:
A powerful magnitude-7.8 earthquake struck the southern Philippines early Monday morning, collapsing buildings and killing at least 32 people while injuring more than 200 others. The quake also generated a 3-foot tsunami that reached nearby coastlines across the region.

The earthquake centered about 8 miles southwest of General Santos City on the island of Mindanao, with a depth of 6.2 miles according to initial reports from the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology. It struck at 7:37 a.m. local time. The US Geological Survey recorded the magnitude as 7.8 with a depth of 34 miles.

Video verified by news organizations showed significant structural damage in General Santos City and surrounding areas. The upper floor of a Jollibee restaurant collapsed, and outer concrete walls of a commercial complex gave way. In Davao del Sur, part of a high school building collapsed as students were gathering outside. A convenience store in General Santos City had its entrance destroyed, with broken glass and overturned benches scattered across the street.

Robert Dagon of the General Santos City police told news agencies that many buildings were affected but officials were focused on ongoing rescue operations. A spokesperson for the civil defense agency reported 19 people feared dead, 134 injured, and 12 missing in initial counts, though these figures were still being verified.

The Pacific Tsunami Warning Center initially warned that waves up to 10 feet were possible on some Philippine coasts and waves up to 3 feet on some Indonesian and Malaysian coastlines. The center later said the threat had largely passed.

Power outages were reported across the affected region, and authorities urged residents to move to higher ground and avoid entering damaged buildings due to the risk of aftershocks. The civil defense office warned of potential dangers from aftershocks following the main quake.

The earthquake struck as public schools were reopening for a new academic year, with students present in several buildings during the tremor. Video from Mahayhay elementary school in Davao showed panicked pupils scrambling for safety during a morning flag ceremony. President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. ordered the suspension of schools in affected areas until further notice, stating that "the safety of our children comes first." The Philippines Red Cross reported providing support to traumatized students at three high schools.

The Philippines sits along the Pacific Ring of Fire, an arc of seismic faults that encircles the Pacific Ocean. This geographic location makes the country one of the world's most disaster-prone nations, regularly experiencing earthquakes and volcanic eruptions. The archipelago also faces approximately 20 typhoons and tropical storms annually.

Government agencies continued assessing damage and clearing routes for rescue operations, with evacuation centers operational across the affected areas.

cards.headline: At Least 32 Dead After Major Earthquake Strikes Southern Philippines
cards.teaser: A 7.8-magnitude earthquake off the island of Mindanao triggered a deadly landslide and small tsunami waves, leaving more than 100 injured and tens of thousands displaced.
cards.body:
A magnitude-7.8 earthquake struck off Mindanao in the southern Philippines on Monday, killing at least 32 people and injuring more than 200 others. The powerful quake collapsed buildings across the region and displaced tens of thousands of residents from their homes.

The earthquake triggered a 3-foot tsunami that affected nearby coasts in the Philippines, Indonesia, and Japan. Emergency responders worked to reach affected communities and conduct ongoing rescue operations in the heavily damaged areas.

cards.headline: Armenian Prime Minister Claims Victory in Election Seen as Test of Russian Influence
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan declared victory in an election viewed as a measure of Russia's sway over the former Soviet republic.
cards.body:
Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan claimed victory in parliamentary elections that were widely seen as a test of Russia's influence in the former Soviet republic. The pro-Europe party's win marks a shift away from Armenia's traditional alignment with Moscow.

The election took place under pressure from Russia, which has long considered Armenia a key ally in the region. Pashinyan's government has moved to strengthen ties with European nations and reduce dependence on Russia for security and economic support. The result signals Armenia's continued pivot toward the West despite Moscow's attempts to maintain its sphere of influence in the South Caucasus.

cards.headline: U.K. Prime Minister Calls on Tech Companies to Block Children From Sharing Intimate Images
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Keir Starmer told Apple and Google they must prevent children from sending nude images on their devices.
cards.body:
British Prime Minister Keir Starmer has given Apple and Google until September to implement software that blocks explicit images on children's phones. The technology would use nudity-detection algorithms or similar solutions to prevent young users from taking or sharing intimate photos unless verified as adults.

Starmer warned that if the companies fail to voluntarily activate these built-in features, the government will pursue legislation to enforce the requirement. The move reflects the U.K. government's broader effort to strengthen protections for children online.

cards.headline: Malawi Repatriates Citizens From South Africa Amid Xenophobia Concerns
cards.teaser: Malawi joined several African nations in transporting citizens out of South Africa following reports of violence against migrants.
cards.body:
Malawi is transporting its citizens out of South Africa following reports of violence against migrants. The repatriation effort comes as multiple African nations take similar steps to bring their people home due to security concerns in the country.

The situation has been intensified by anti-immigration campaigns in South Africa. A protest movement called March & March has organized rallies against illegal immigration and has demanded that undocumented migrants leave the country by June 30. African migrants report living in extreme fear, saying that legal status offers little protection as xenophobic sentiment continues to spread.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Fall on Tech Sell-Off and Middle East Escalation
cards.teaser: Markets in Europe and Asia declined as technology stocks dropped and oil prices rose following strikes between Iran and Israel.
cards.body:
Stock markets in Europe and Asia declined on Monday following a sharp sell-off in US technology stocks the previous week. Investors grew concerned about whether major technology firms leading the artificial intelligence boom could sustain their substantial spending plans.

Oil prices rose as Iran and Israel exchanged military strikes, reigniting Middle East tensions. The renewed conflict dampened expectations for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, raising fresh concerns about potential energy supply disruptions from the region.

cards.headline: Pakistan District Faces Extreme Heat as Temperatures Reach 125 Degrees
cards.teaser: Residents of Dadu District in Pakistan searched for shade as temperatures climbed to dangerous levels in an area prone to sandstorms, drought, and flooding.
cards.body:
Original Card Text

People in Dadu District, Pakistan, struggled to find shade as temperatures reached 125 degrees. The area faces extreme weather conditions each season, including sandstorms, drought, and flooding.

The punishing heat adds to the challenges residents face in a region already vulnerable to environmental crises. Pakistan has experienced increasingly severe heatwaves in recent years, straining infrastructure and posing health risks to populations with limited access to cooling or reliable electricity.

cards.headline: Pope calls for moral renewal in address to Spanish parliament
cards.teaser: The American pope addressed the Spanish legislature for the first time, demanding respect for human dignity in public life.
cards.body:
In a historic first papal address to the Spanish legislature, the pope urged lawmakers and public officials to pursue moral renewal in their institutions and public life. He stressed the importance of protecting the inherent dignity of all people through their work in government.

The pope's remarks to Spanish legislators represented a direct call for political leaders to prioritize human dignity in their policy decisions and legislative efforts.

cards.headline: Former USAID official publishes account of agency under Trump administration
cards.teaser: Nicholas Enrich, who served at USAID under four administrations, released a book detailing his experiences as a self-described whistleblower.
cards.body:
Nicholas Enrich, a longtime staff member at the U.S. Agency for International Development who worked under four administrations, has published a book titled "Into the Woodchipper: A Whistleblower's Account of How the Trump Administration Shredded USAID." In the book, Enrich describes his experiences at the agency and discusses topics including the agency's work on Ebola.

Drawing on his tenure across multiple presidential administrations, Enrich offers a perspective on how USAID operated during the Trump years compared to other periods of his employment at the agency.

cards.headline: Maine Democratic candidates open to changing electoral vote system
cards.teaser: Three Democratic gubernatorial candidates in Maine said they would consider ending the state's unique method of allocating presidential electoral votes.
cards.body:
Three Democratic candidates for Maine governor indicated openness to ending the state's distinctive presidential election system. The candidates received an endorsement from the Platner family, a politically influential group in the state, and face questions about their positions on electoral reform.

Maine is one of two states that splits electoral votes by congressional district rather than awarding all votes to the statewide winner. The Democratic candidates' willingness to reconsider this system comes amid broader discussions about electoral vote allocation, with Nebraska Republicans also considering changes to their similar split-vote system.

cards.headline: Republican candidate narrowly misses Los Angeles mayoral runoff
cards.teaser: Spencer Pratt failed to advance to the Los Angeles mayoral runoff as Nithya Raman overtook him in the latest vote count.
cards.body:
Spencer Pratt did not qualify for the Los Angeles mayoral runoff election, with the latest results showing Nithya Raman moving ahead of him in the vote count. Republican officials criticized the outcome amid broader disputes over California election procedures.

A U.S. attorney has accused California of blocking a voter roll audit, and federal prosecutors are pursuing multiple election fraud investigations in the state. Former President Trump called the California primary results rigged, though election officials have defended the integrity of the voting process.

cards.headline: Polling shows farmers turning against Trump ahead of midterms
cards.teaser: Key voters in the Midwest, including farmers who previously supported Trump, are showing signs of dissatisfaction with the former president.
cards.body:
Farmers in the Midwest are expressing frustration with former President Trump, according to recent reports. The discontent among agricultural workers, traditionally loyal Republican voters, could affect party performance in upcoming midterm elections.

Farmers face ongoing economic struggles that are testing their political loyalty to the Republican Party. Opinion writers and analysts describe Trump as having betrayed agricultural workers, with some voters indicating readiness to support alternative candidates in future elections.

hero.headline: Global stocks fall as tech sector sells off and Middle East tensions escalate
hero.body:
Stock markets across Europe and Asia declined sharply on Monday as technology shares experienced a significant downturn and renewed military conflict between Iran and Israel unsettled investors. The twin pressures of sector-specific weakness and geopolitical risk created turbulent trading conditions worldwide.

The technology sell-off reflected growing investor concerns about valuations in the artificial intelligence sector. Major chip manufacturers saw substantial losses, with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix dropping 9% and 6% respectively in South Korea. The South Korean Kospi index fell nearly 9% at one point, forcing a brief trading suspension. In Japan, the Nikkei 225 declined 3%, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell 1.5%. European tech companies also suffered steep losses early in the day, with semiconductor firms like ASML down 3.2% and BESI down 4.5%, while German chip equipment maker Aixtron dropped nearly 6%.

The market weakness came after a sharp sell-off in US technology stocks the previous Friday, when the Nasdaq index lost nearly 5% and the S&P 500 fell 2%, ending nine weeks of consecutive gains. Investors expressed growing nervousness about the spending plans of major technology companies pursuing artificial intelligence development. According to Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, concerns had intensified around higher inflation and potential interest rate rises. "Tech giants with deep cash pockets are seeking fresh funding to finance eye-watering capital expenditure plans," she noted, adding that worries exist about whether assets invested today at current high prices could become obsolete.

Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo investment bank, suggested the correction reflected a shift in investor sentiment. "The market is becoming more selective on AI," Chanana said. "Investors now want clearer proof of earnings delivery, monetisation, capex discipline and funding returns."

The escalation of Middle East hostilities added a second layer of concern to markets. Iran and Israel exchanged direct military strikes, raising fears about the stability of a fragile ceasefire arrangement. Oil prices initially surged nearly 5% to $97.60 per barrel as traders assessed potential disruptions to energy supplies. Brent crude later retreated to $94.60 per barrel after Iran announced it was halting military operations against Israel, following statements from Donald Trump calling for both sides to cease military action immediately.

In London, the FTSE 100 opened down 0.4%, with airlines and aerospace companies among the biggest fallers. However, oil firms BP and Shell gained on expectations of higher energy prices. German, French and Spanish markets also declined before recovering some losses as the Middle East situation stabilized. US markets were expected to open higher on Monday as investor sentiment improved following de-escalation signals from both Iran and Israel.

Taking equity positions in private companies would represent an unusual intervention in the market by the federal government, raising questions about the relationship between Washington and Silicon Valley.

cards.headline: Weight loss drug maker shares sink on safety concerns
cards.teaser: A pharmaceutical company developing obesity treatments saw its stock price drop 25 percent after releasing new clinical safety data that concerned investors.
cards.body:
Shares of a weight loss drug manufacturer tumbled 25% after the company released new safety data from clinical trials. The data revealed that approximately one in five patients stopped taking survodutide, an experimental obesity medication being developed with Boehringer, due to side effects.

The discontinuation rate prompted investor concerns about the drug's tolerability relative to competing medications in its class. The stock decline reflected worries about the treatment's commercial viability and safety profile compared to other options available to patients.

cards.headline: Eli Lilly shares rise on successful obesity drug trial results
cards.teaser: The pharmaceutical company's stock gained in premarket trading after reporting positive late-stage trial data for a next-generation weight loss medication.
cards.body:
Eli Lilly announced successful results from a late-stage clinical trial of retatrutide, an experimental obesity drug. The medication demonstrated significant weight loss and other health benefits, including improvements in sleep apnea and blood sugar control.

The trial data showed patients lost approximately 30 percent of their body weight, setting a high benchmark in the competitive obesity drug market. The positive results boosted investor confidence in the company's pipeline of weight loss treatments.

cards.headline: European economic recovery faces extended slowdown
cards.teaser: Europe's economic outlook has dimmed as the conflict in Iran continues, with indicators pointing to sustained higher prices and weaker growth.
cards.body:
Europe is confronting the prospect of a prolonged period of economic difficulty rather than a swift recovery. Ongoing conflict in Iran has contributed to a deteriorating outlook, with economists expecting both elevated prices and subdued growth to persist.

The economic challenges facing the continent have intensified as geopolitical instability continues. Rather than experiencing a quick shock followed by recovery, European economies appear headed for an extended phase of slower expansion and inflationary pressure.

cards.headline: UK government pushes Apple and Google to block explicit content on children's devices
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Keir Starmer called on major tech companies to activate built-in features preventing children from accessing sexually explicit images on their phones.
cards.body:
Prime Minister Keir Starmer has given Apple and Google until September to activate software that blocks explicit images on children's phones. The companies must implement nudity-detection algorithms or other technical solutions to prevent minors from accessing or sharing sexually explicit content, or face legislation mandating the requirement.

Both firms have already developed the necessary tools to detect and filter such material on smartphones and tablets. Starmer's directive represents an escalation in the government's effort to enforce stronger protections for young users online, moving from requests to threats of regulatory action.

hero.headline: Astronomers identify source of repeating radio signals from space
hero.body:
A student astronomer has identified the source of mysterious radio signals that have been pinging from space in regular intervals. The signals, which repeat every 1.4 hours, have puzzled scientists who detected them coming from deep space. Researchers describe the discovery as a Rosetta stone for understanding these cosmic transmissions.

The periodic signals originate from an accreting white dwarf binary system, according to findings published in Nature. White dwarfs are the dense remnants of stars that have exhausted their nuclear fuel. In a binary system, material from a companion star falls onto the white dwarf, releasing energy in the process. The regular timing of the emissions corresponds to the orbital period of the two stars.

The signals manifest as both radio waves and X-rays, allowing astronomers to observe them across multiple wavelengths. This dual emission pattern provided crucial clues that helped researchers pinpoint the white dwarf binary as the source. The discovery resolves a longstanding mystery about these repeating cosmic signals that had been detected but not explained.

White dwarf binaries are common in the universe, but this particular system exhibits unusual characteristics in how it releases energy. The findings help astronomers better understand how matter behaves under extreme gravitational conditions and how energy is released when material accretes onto compact stellar objects. The research team credits the student astronomer with making the key observations that led to identifying the source.

The discovery provides scientists with a new tool for studying stellar remnants and binary star systems. By observing the precise timing and characteristics of these signals, researchers can learn more about the physics of accretion and the behavior of matter in extreme environments. The white dwarf binary will likely become a target for further study as astronomers work to understand the mechanisms producing these regular emissions.

cards.headline: Uber opens waitlist for Wayve robotaxis in London
cards.teaser: Uber customers in the UK can now join an interest list to ride in Wayve autonomous vehicles.
cards.body:
Uber has opened an interest list for London customers interested in riding Wayve robotaxis. Those who sign up will have a better chance of being matched with a Wayve autonomous vehicle once the service launches later this year.

Wayve is a UK-based autonomous driving company using machine learning to develop self-driving technology. The partnership positions Uber to compete with Waymo in the robotaxi market, with London serving as a key testing ground for one of Uber's largest markets.

cards.headline: Apple holds internal meeting on AI strategy ahead of developer conference
cards.teaser: A 2025 meeting at Apple reportedly set the company's current direction for AI and Siri improvements.
cards.body:
Apple held a meeting in 2025 that determined the company's approach to artificial intelligence and voice assistant development. The session put Apple Intelligence and Siri on their current development path, according to reports ahead of the company's developer conference.

Tim Cook is focusing significant time on AI initiatives as Apple works to address criticism of Siri's performance compared to competitors. The company is expected to announce updates to its AI strategy at its developer conference, giving Apple what some describe as a second attempt to demonstrate progress in artificial intelligence.

cards.headline: Microsoft demonstrates Surface Laptop Ultra at Computex
cards.teaser: Microsoft showed a new Surface Laptop Ultra model at the computing industry trade show.
cards.body:
Microsoft presented the Surface Laptop Ultra at Computex, the annual computer hardware trade show. Observers who tested the device said it demonstrates the company's commitment to the product line.

The announcement comes as Nvidia pushes into AI-powered personal computers with new laptop chips. Nvidia introduced the RTX Spark as its most efficient PC chip and announced partnerships with Microsoft to integrate AI features into Windows PCs. The companies are betting on demand for AI capabilities in personal computers beyond specialized use cases.

cards.headline: Prada designs cooling undergarment for NASA Artemis astronauts
cards.teaser: The luxury fashion house created technical undergarments for moon missions in partnership with Axiom Space.
cards.body:
Prada and Axiom Space have unveiled a liquid cooling and ventilation garment (LCVG) that astronauts will wear beneath their spacesuits during the Artemis IV mission to the moon in 2028. The high-tech undergarment serves as a critical base layer designed to regulate body temperature in the lunar environment.

The collaboration between the Italian luxury brand and Axiom Space represents Prada's entry into the aerospace industry. The LCVG will be worn under the Axiom Extravehicular Mobility Unit (AxEMU) spacesuit, combining fashion design expertise with functional aerospace engineering for NASA's lunar exploration program.

cards.headline: Gears of War: E-Day launches in October as Xbox console exclusive
cards.teaser: The latest Gears of War title will be available on Xbox Series X/S and PC this fall.
cards.body:
Microsoft confirmed that Gears of War: E-Day will launch in October as an Xbox console exclusive, with a PC version also available. The announcement came during the Xbox Games Showcase, where the company revealed the game will not be coming to PlayStation 5, despite previous rumors suggesting a multiplatform release.

The showcase featured the game's dedicated presentation alongside announcements for other upcoming Xbox titles.

hero.headline: Christian Eriksen Stable After Collapsing During Denmark Friendly
hero.body:
Denmark midfielder Christian Eriksen collapsed on the pitch during a friendly match against Ukraine on Sunday and was taken to the hospital, but he was conscious when he left the field. The match in Odense was abandoned following the medical emergency.

The 34-year-old player, who experienced cardiac arrest during a European Championship match in 2021, regained consciousness quickly after the incident. Denmark's national team doctor Morten Boesen said Eriksen was briefly unconscious but recovered rapidly and even walked off the pitch by himself.

"The pacemaker responded as it should," Boesen said after the incident. "Christian is doing well, and he asked me to send his regards to all the players and tell them that he was okay."

Eriksen will undergo further examinations at the hospital to determine what caused the collapse. The Danish Football Association confirmed that he is in good spirits and is expected to be discharged soon.

Eriksen was fitted with an implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD) after his 2021 cardiac arrest. This device is designed to reset the heart after a cardiac event and allowed him to resume his professional career at both club and international level. The device functioned properly during Sunday's incident.

Players from both Denmark and Ukraine formed a protective ring around Eriksen while medics treated him on the field. Medical personnel responded swiftly to the emergency, reflecting football's commitment to player safety in such situations.

Denmark's captain Pierre-Emile Højbjerg praised the quick response. "I turned around and saw Christian on his way to the floor," he told Danish broadcaster TV2. "Everyone reacted super-fast and with respect. I can only compliment how much courage those who took care of Christian on the field had. The most important thing is that Christian is doing well."

The former Tottenham and Manchester United midfielder has had a remarkable recovery since his first cardiac arrest. After that 2021 incident, he told the BBC that he remembered everything except the five minutes he was unconscious. He recalled hearing medics in the ambulance mention he had been unconscious for five minutes.

This latest incident occurred during an end-of-season friendly between two nations that did not qualify for the World Cup. The collapse in the 65th minute prompted immediate medical attention and led to the match being called off.

Eriksen's ability to continue playing professional football following such a serious medical condition has been closely monitored by medical staff and football authorities. His case has heightened awareness about cardiac screening and emergency preparedness at football matches across Europe.

cards.headline: Leclerc Calls Ferrari Brake Failure Dangerous After Monaco Crash
cards.teaser: Charles Leclerc criticized Ferrari after a brake failure caused him to crash out of the Monaco Grand Prix while running in podium position.
cards.body:
Charles Leclerc crashed out of the Monaco Grand Prix after experiencing a critical brake failure late in the race. Running in a podium position, the Ferrari driver lost control and hit the barriers when three of his four brakes failed to work.

Following the incident, Leclerc described the brake issue as "borderline dangerous." The mechanical failure cost him a potential podium finish at his home race in Monaco, with BBC F1 correspondent Andrew Benson reporting on the driver's comments during The Chequered Flag Podcast.

cards.headline: Patriots Acquire Wide Receiver A.J. Brown in Trade
cards.teaser: The New England Patriots traded for wide receiver A.J. Brown, adding a veteran playmaker to their offense.
cards.body:
The Patriots completed a trade to acquire wide receiver A.J. Brown, bringing the veteran pass catcher to New England. The move addresses a need in the Patriots receiving corps and gives the team an established target.

Brown is expected to play a significant role in New England's offense after the trade. The acquisition marks a notable addition for the Patriots as they look to strengthen their passing attack.

cards.headline: Charley Hull Finishes Strong at U.S. Women's Open
cards.teaser: Charley Hull came close to winning her first major title at the U.S. Women's Open, shooting a record 65 at Riviera.
cards.body:
Charley Hull came agonizingly close to winning her first major championship at the U.S. Women's Open at Riviera, finishing second after a strong performance throughout the tournament. The British golfer's near-miss has drawn attention from analysts who believe a major victory may be imminent.

Nelly Korda ultimately claimed the title by one shot over Hull and Gaby Lopez, securing her second consecutive major victory and fourth major title overall. Korda's winning putt on the 18th green dramatically caught the cup's edge before dropping in, a dramatic finish that denied Hull the championship she came so close to capturing.

cards.headline: Tuchel Says Bellingham Must Fight for England Starting Spot
cards.teaser: England manager Thomas Tuchel indicated Jude Bellingham will need to compete for a place in the starting lineup at the World Cup.
cards.body:
England manager Thomas Tuchel has stated that Jude Bellingham will need to compete for his place in the starting lineup at the World Cup. The comments underscore that the midfielder's position is not guaranteed despite his previous regular appearances for the national team.

Tuchel's remarks suggest he is exploring various midfield options as he prepares the squad for the tournament.

cards.headline: NBA Finals Tickets at Madison Square Garden Reach Record Prices
cards.teaser: Ticket prices for NBA Finals games at Madison Square Garden have reached levels exceeding nearly every Super Bowl, creating difficult choices for season ticket holders.
cards.body:
Knicks season ticket holders are facing difficult decisions as NBA Finals seats command thousands of dollars. Tickets for Games 3 and 4 at Madison Square Garden between the Knicks and Spurs have reached prices higher than nearly every NFL Super Bowl. Knicks player Josh Hart commented on the situation, calling the Finals ticket prices for fans wanting to attend at MSG ridiculous.

The Spurs enter Game 3 down 2-0 in the best-of-seven series. Star player Victor Wembanyama expressed confidence in his team's ability to mount a comeback, saying he is embracing both the setbacks and success. The San Antonio team faces a hostile environment at Madison Square Garden as the series continues.

cards.headline: McCullum Backs Stokes to Regain Batting Form
cards.teaser: England head coach Brendon McCullum expressed confidence that captain Ben Stokes will soon return to form with the bat.
cards.body:
England head coach Brendon McCullum has backed captain Ben Stokes to rediscover his batting form, saying the all-rounder is "not too far away" from a return to runs. Stokes has struggled with the bat in recent matches while captaining the Test side.

McCullum's public support comes after England's first Test victory since the Ashes, a win against New Zealand at Lord's. The head coach praised his players' resilience in moving past their disappointing Australian campaign, highlighting their ability to maintain their attacking approach despite difficult batting conditions.

hero.headline: Grammy-Winning Musician Killed
hero.body:
Jazz musician and composer Chuck Mangione has died at age 84. He passed away peacefully in his sleep at his home in Rochester, New York on July 22, 2025, according to a statement from his family released to the Rochester Democrat and Chronicle.

Mangione was born on November 29, 1940, in Rochester. He grew up in a household filled with jazz music, introduced to the genre by his father at an early age. His father would play jazz albums and take young Chuck and his brother Gap to Sunday afternoon jazz performances at local clubs. The family home became a gathering place for accomplished jazz musicians, with artists like Carmen McRae and Art Blakey visiting for meals.

Mangione began his musical career in high school, playing trumpet in a jazz band called the Jazz Brothers alongside his brother. He went on to study at the Eastman School of Music, graduating in 1963 with a degree in music. He later returned to the school in 1968 to direct its jazz ensemble and help develop the institution's jazz program until 1972.

His solo career proved highly successful. Mangione released more than 30 albums and sold millions of records worldwide. His 1977 album "Feels So Good" became one of the most successful jazz records ever made. Mangione received 13 Grammy nominations and won two Grammy Awards, one in 1977 for "Bellavia" and another in 1979 for "The Children of Sanchez."

Beyond his commercial achievements, Mangione was recognized for his contributions to music and culture. He performed at the closing ceremony of the 1980 Winter Olympics in Lake Placid. In 2009, he donated music memorabilia to the Smithsonian National Museum of American History. He was inducted into the Rochester Music Hall of Fame in 2012.

Mangione was known for his work on the flugelhorn and trumpet. His family described his relationship with music as characterized by "boundless energy, unabashed enthusiasm, and pure joy that radiated from the stage." They emphasized his genuine appreciation for his fans worldwide, noting that he would remain at the edge of the stage after concerts for as long as needed to sign autographs and meet supporters.

In their statement, his family said, "Chuck's love affair with music has been characterized by his boundless energy, unabashed enthusiasm, and pure joy that radiated from the stage." They added that his dedication to his audience was evident in his willingness to connect with fans after performances.

His death marks the loss of a significant figure in jazz music who helped shape the genre while maintaining deep roots in his hometown of Rochester.

cards.headline: Ali Louis Bourzgui, Joshua Henry, and Caissie Levy Win at 2026 Tony Awards
cards.teaser: The 2026 Tony Awards recognized performers and productions across multiple categories.
cards.body:
Ali Louis Bourzgui, Joshua Henry, and Caissie Levy were among the winners at the 2026 Tony Awards. The ceremony also recognized achievements from established performers, including John Lithgow and Laurie Metcalf. Schmigadoon! emerged as a major winner at the awards.

Pink hosted the ceremony, which celebrated excellence in Broadway theater. The event featured performances and appearances that highlighted both seasoned and emerging talent in American theater.

cards.headline: Fox Secures NFL Broadcasting Rights in Mexico
cards.teaser: Fox Corp. will broadcast NFL games in Mexico, including Thursday Night Football and the Super Bowl.
cards.body:
Fox Corp. announced a new agreement to show NFL games through its Mexican outlets. The deal includes broadcasting rights for Thursday Night Football and the Super Bowl, expanding the league's reach in Mexico.

The agreement represents continued deal-making between the NFL and U.S. media companies. Fox will provide Mexican audiences with access to a wider range of American football content through its broadcast channels. The move reflects ongoing efforts to grow the sport's audience in Mexico, where interest in American football has been increasing.

cards.headline: Idris Elba Addresses James Bond Casting Speculation
cards.teaser: Actor Idris Elba said rumors linking him to the James Bond role were never legitimate.
cards.body:
Idris Elba has dismissed speculation about him playing James Bond, telling British GQ that the rumors were "never legit" and "not realistic." The 53-year-old actor, currently promoting Masters of the Universe, refuted claims he was seriously considered to replace Daniel Craig in the 007 role after Craig's 2021 departure.

Elba stated that audiences would not accept a Black actor in the iconic role, suggesting cultural preferences work against such casting. He has also pushed back against making the character "woke," effectively closing the door on years of fan and media speculation about his potential involvement with the franchise.

cards.headline: Hugh Laurie Defends House Against Criticism of Repetitive Format
cards.teaser: Hugh Laurie responded to criticism that his medical drama followed the same narrative structure each episode.
cards.body:
Hugh Laurie has defended House against criticism that the show followed a repetitive narrative pattern. The actor, who starred in the Fox medical drama from 2004 to 2012, responded to a critic who claimed the show had the same structure every episode.

Laurie said that if viewers only saw hospital and medical content, then the show was not meant for them. His comments came in response to a critic who went viral on social media over the weekend. The English actor remains a strong defender of the series more than a decade after it ended its eight-season run.

cards.headline: The Voice Winner to Perform at 2027 Governors Ball
cards.teaser: The Season 30 winner of The Voice will receive a main stage performance slot at the 2027 Governors Ball music festival.
cards.body:
NBC's The Voice has partnered with Live Nation Studios and the Governors Ball festival to offer its next winner a major performance opportunity. The Season 30 champion will perform on the main stage at the 2027 Governors Ball.

The arrangement provides the winning contestant with a high-profile booking before their victory. The partnership between the singing competition and the music festival represents a collaboration between television and live music industries. Governors Ball is a major annual music festival that features established and emerging artists.

cards.headline: Guns N' Roses to Play Two Indian Cities in November
cards.teaser: The rock band will perform in Bengaluru and Guwahati as part of their ongoing world tour.
cards.body:
Guns N' Roses will return to India for two concerts in November. The band will perform at Nice Grounds in Bengaluru on Nov. 14 and Khanapara Ground in Guwahati on Nov. 16.

The shows are part of the Asia leg of their ongoing world tour. BookMyShow Live is producing and promoting both concerts. This marks another return to India for the American rock band, which continues to tour internationally.

hero.headline: Trump says Israel must accept any Iran deal, calls for immediate ceasefire
hero.body:
President Trump asserted his authority over Middle East negotiations, telling the Financial Times that Israel will be forced to accept whatever agreement the United States reaches with Iran. "I call all the shots. He doesn't call the shots," Trump said, referring to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The statement came as Israel and Iran engaged in direct military strikes for the first time since a ceasefire took effect in April. Israel targeted petrochemical facilities in Mahshahr that produce materials for ballistic missile development. Iran responded by backing its proxy Hezbollah after Israeli military operations escalated in Lebanon.

Trump called for an immediate halt to hostilities on Truth Social, posting that "Israel and Iran must immediately stop shooting" and urging both sides to stand down as regional tensions mounted.

The Trump administration's approach signals a significant shift in US policy toward Israel. By publicly stating he controls negotiations regardless of Israeli objections, Trump indicated the administration intends to pursue talks with Iran without requiring Israeli approval. This contrasts with previous administrations that granted Israel substantial influence over Iran-related decisions.

However, divisions have emerged between the Trump administration and allied nations over ceasefire terms. Vice President JD Vance clarified in Budapest that Lebanon was not part of the Iran ceasefire agreement, despite apparent misunderstandings. He stated: "I think the Iranians thought that the ceasefire included Lebanon, and it just didn't. We never made that promise."

British officials have publicly disagreed with this position. Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper told BBC Radio 4 that continued Israeli strikes on Lebanon were "completely wrong" and emphasized that "Lebanon must be included in the ceasefire." Defence Secretary John Healey similarly called for ending the Israel-Lebanon conflict as part of broader ceasefire terms.

Britain also expressed concerns about Trump's suggestion that Iran could charge tolls for passage through the Strait of Hormuz. Healey warned that introducing any pay-for-passage system would create a dangerous precedent for international shipping and contradict established maritime law. He said such an arrangement "simply isn't sensible and isn't actually doable."

The escalation in Lebanon has intensified since the April ceasefire announcement. Israeli bombing campaigns have continued with significant casualties, while Iran responded by halting oil tanker passage through the Strait of Hormuz. The blockade of this critical shipping route has affected global fuel and fertilizer prices, with ripple effects on economies worldwide.

Cooper emphasized in her remarks to City leaders that freedom of navigation through international waterways underpins global trade and security. The renewed hostilities and diplomatic disagreements between the Trump administration and its traditional allies suggest that achieving a sustainable ceasefire agreement faces considerable obstacles, despite Trump's insistence on American control over negotiations.

cards.headline: Hawley criticizes four Republicans who voted against voter ID bill in reconciliation package
cards.teaser: Senator Josh Hawley is criticizing four GOP senators who voted against adding the SAVE America Act to a budget reconciliation package.
cards.body:
Senator Josh Hawley of Missouri criticized four Republican senators who voted against a motion to add the SAVE America Act to a $70 billion budget reconciliation package. Hawley said he could not understand why fellow Republicans would vote against a voter ID law.

The four Republicans who opposed the motion were Senators Susan Collins of Maine, Mitch McConnell of Kentucky, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska, and a fourth senator. The vote effectively blocked the voter identification legislation from being included in the larger budget bill that Republicans are advancing through the reconciliation process.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: Former Biden administration official Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary in New Mexico's gubernatorial race.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, who served as an official in the Biden administration, won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico. Her victory positions her as the party's nominee in the general election.

If elected in November, Haaland would make history as the first female Native American governor in the United States. The general election will determine whether she achieves that milestone.

cards.headline: FISA Section 702 spy law faces Friday deadline as extension remains uncertain
cards.teaser: The Section 702 surveillance law expires this Friday, with chances of an extension uncertain.
cards.body:
Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act is set to expire on Friday, and the prospects for extending the law remain unclear. The uncertainty is partly attributed to Trump's Director of National Intelligence appointment.

The spy law has been a key tool for intelligence gathering, but its renewal has faced political obstacles. With only days remaining before expiration, Congress has not yet secured the votes needed to extend the program.

cards.headline: Bass and Raman advance to runoff in Los Angeles mayoral race
cards.teaser: Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass will face progressive candidate Nithya Raman in a runoff election after Raman advanced past GOP candidate Spencer Pratt.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass and progressive challenger Nithya Raman will compete in a runoff election for mayor after Raman was projected to advance. Raman overtook Spencer Pratt, a Republican candidate and former reality television star, to secure her place in the runoff.

The Bass campaign criticized Raman over homeless policy, saying she had not done enough to reduce homeless encampments near schools. The runoff will determine who leads Los Angeles for the next term.

cards.headline: Hilton and Becerra lead in California governor primary
cards.teaser: Republicans Steve Hilton and Chad Bianco and Democrats Xavier Becerra, Katie Porter, and Tom Steyer are competing to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Steve Hilton and Xavier Becerra are leading in California's gubernatorial primary as results come in. Republicans Steve Hilton and Chad Bianco are competing against Democrats Katie Porter, Tom Steyer, and Xavier Becerra for their party nominations.

The winner will replace Governor Gavin Newsom, who is not seeking another term. California's primary system allows the top two vote-getters to advance to the general election regardless of party affiliation.

cards.headline: Loophole allows wealthy households to qualify for SNAP benefits
cards.teaser: A federal loophole in the SNAP program permits households with significant assets to qualify for food assistance.
cards.body:
A loophole in the federal Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program allows households with significant assets to qualify for food assistance benefits. The gap in eligibility rules permits millionaires to receive SNAP benefits intended for low-income Americans.

The loophole diverts resources from those who need assistance and costs taxpayers billions of dollars. Critics argue the program's asset verification rules need reform to ensure aid reaches only those with genuine financial need.
